title: Revenue per seat mile pulled further ahead of cost
question: After accounting for a common seat-mile denominator, did operating revenue pull ahead of all-in operating expense?
unit: US cents per available seat mile
comparability_limits: RASM equals operating revenue divided by available seat miles; CASM equals operating expenses divided by the same available seat miles. Both rows cover the three months ended September 30.
The difference in cents per seat mile is a unit operating spread, not net margin, cash flow or an EPS forecast. Rounding of reported inputs limits precision.
CASM includes fuel and all reported operating expenses. Company-defined CASM-X excludes fuel, special items and profit sharing and must not be labelled all-in cost.
Reported cost and profit quality may reflect asset-sale and sale-leaseback gains. A wider reported spread alone does not establish recurring operating strength.

Use two labelled horizontal dumbbells with connectors only between revenue and cost within the same quarter, not a time-series line. Shared linear scale, a clearly disclosed axis extent and exact two-decimal endpoint labels are required; no bar-shaped marks on a truncated baseline.

Mobile layout: two generous rows, direct endpoint labels with collision avoidance, and a concise legend above the plot. Do not enlarge the tiny prior-year spread into an unlabelled visual exaggeration.

series.name: All-in operating expense per seat mile (CASM)
